Recede

/rih-SEED/ — rhymes with 'seed' · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To recede is to gradually move back or withdraw from a previous position, becoming more distant over time.

Once the floodwaters receded, the cleanup began.

Worked Example

As winter passed and spring arrived, the snow line receded higher up the mountain, revealing the green meadows that had been buried beneath it.

Recede is more precise than 'melt' or 'disappear' because it emphasizes the movement—the snow isn't just gone, it has moved backward and upward. The word captures the spatial retreat, showing what was hidden is now visible.

How Recede Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

retreat

retreat: to move back, often away from danger

withdraw

withdraw: to pull back or remove oneself deliberately

shrink

shrink: to become smaller in size or extent

Antonyms

advance

advance: to move forward and gain ground

approach

approach: to come nearer in space or time

How Strong Is It? — withdraw → retreat → flee → recede

withdraw vs. recede

withdraw vs. recede: Withdraw is a gentler, more deliberate cousin of recede: a person quietly withdraws from a conversation, while waters and shorelines recede gradually on their own.

retreat vs. recede

retreat vs. recede: Retreat is more forceful than recede; an army retreats under pressure, while a glacier simply recedes, drawing back slowly with no battle at all.

flee vs. recede

flee vs. recede: Flee is the strongest of the four — running away in urgent panic — far more dramatic than to recede, which is a slow, steady drawing back.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — re-

Prefix — re-: back (Latin)

Root — cede

Root — cede: to go; to yield (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Re- means 'back' and the Latin root cede means 'to go' — so to recede is literally 'to go back,' which is why floodwaters, hairlines, and glaciers all recede: they withdraw from ground they once held.

Use the root in a new word: proceed

Use the root in a new word: proceed: When the light turned green, the cars could proceed — 'go forward' — the exact opposite direction of recede, 'go back.'

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Recede is precise when something physically moves backward or away gradually—hairlines, coastlines, floodwaters, borders, tides. For something simply moving backward or away intentionally, 'retreat' or 'withdraw' works fine. For something moving away hastily in escape, 'flee' is better.
